claims.text: The starting cermet contains 70 wt% ZrB2 and 30 wt% of an equimolar Al-Fe-Ni-Co-Cr binder.
The ZrB2 powder has greater than 99.8% purity and a particle size of 1–5 μm.
SPS at 1500 °C optimizes binder fluidity in the ZrB2-AlFeNiCoCr cermet.
At 1500 °C, the high-entropy-alloy binder becomes sufficiently liquid to fill pores uniformly.
Binder fluidity at 1500 °C promotes strong bonding between ZrB2 grains.
Sintering at 1500 °C produces a compact microstructure with approximately 97.71% relative density.
Enhanced pore filling reduces penetration pathways for molten aluminum.
Improved grain bonding minimizes detachment of ZrB2 grains.
Reduced molten-aluminum penetration pathways lower the corrosion rate.
Improved pore filling and grain bonding reduce wear volume.
Improved pore filling and grain bonding increase hardness.
Improved pore filling and grain bonding increase fracture toughness.
The cermet sintered at 1500 °C will have higher relative density than otherwise identical cermets sintered at 1300, 1400, or 1600 °C.
The cermet sintered at 1500 °C will have greater hardness than otherwise identical cermets sintered at 1300, 1400, or 1600 °C.
The cermet sintered at 1500 °C will have greater fracture toughness than otherwise identical cermets sintered at 1300, 1400, or 1600 °C.
The cermet sintered at 1500 °C will have a lower molten-aluminum corrosion rate than otherwise identical cermets sintered at 1300, 1400, or 1600 °C.
The cermet sintered at 1500 °C will have lower wear volume than otherwise identical cermets sintered at 1300, 1400, or 1600 °C.
Pure ZrB2 has a fracture toughness of approximately 4.5 MPa·m^1/2.
Binder loss occurs at a sintering temperature of 1600 °C.
The predicted corrosion benefit remains effective for molten-aluminum exposure at 700 °C for up to 12 days under the specified composition and SPS conditions.
